question: -What is the change of state from liquid to solid at atmospheric pressure known as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Solidification**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Solidification** is the process by which a substance changes its state from a **liquid to a solid**. This typically occurs when the liquid is cooled to its freezing point.
 
• The freezing point is the temperature at which the liquid and solid phases of a substance coexist in equilibrium. For water, this temperature is **0°C (273.15 K)** at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• In the case of solidification, the **molecules of the liquid lose kinetic energy** due to cooling. As a result, they slow down and arrange themselves into a fixed, orderly structure, forming a solid.
 
• Solidification is an **exothermic process**, meaning it releases heat as the liquid transitions into a solid state.
 
• This process is a key principle in various natural phenomena and industrial applications, such as the formation of ice, the casting of metals, and the crystallization of substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Deposition:** 
 
 
• Deposition is the **direct change of state from gas to solid** without passing through the liquid phase.
 
• An example of deposition is the formation of frost, where water vapor in the air turns directly into ice on cold surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation:**
 
 
• Sublimation refers to the change of state from a **solid to a gas** without passing through the liquid phase.
 
• An example of sublimation is the transformation of dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) directly into carbon dioxide gas.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• Evaporation is the process where a liquid changes to a gas at a temperature **below its boiling point**.
 
• It occurs at the surface of the liquid and is responsible for phenomena like drying of clothes and the cooling effect of sweat.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Solidification:**
 
 
• **Metal casting:** The process of shaping metals involves pouring molten metal into molds and allowing it to solidify.
 
• **Ice formation:** Solidification occurs naturally when water is cooled below its freezing point, forming ice.
 
• **Crystallization:** In industries, solidification is used to extract pure solid crystals from a solution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Freezing vs. Solidification:** 
 
 
• Freezing is a specific type of solidification that occurs when a liquid turns into a solid at its freezing point.
 
• Solidification is a more general term that can apply to any liquid turning into a solid, regardless of the temperature or conditions.
 
 
 
• **Latent Heat of Fusion:**
 
 
• The **latent heat of fusion** is the amount of heat energy required to change a unit mass of a substance from solid to liquid (or vice versa) at constant temperature.
 
• For water, the latent heat of fusion is approximately **334 J/g**.
 
 
 
• **Phase Changes and Thermodynamics:**
 
 
• All phase changes, including solidification, involve the transfer of energy in the form of heat.
 
• During solidification, the system releases heat to its surroundings, which is why it is classified as an **exothermic process**.
